Shadow analysis, solar studies, and design envelopes for SketchUp — made by designers, for designers.
Powerful shadow analysis toolbox for SketchUp.

Parasolv is a full suite of tools to generate fast, accurate, an visually compelling shadow studies, all without ever leaving SketchUp. Built for professionals, but with a simple interface anyone can use.
Screenshot: Parasolv Advanced Mode with shadow-fan overlay on a mid-rise massing
Every tool a shadow study needs, right inside SketchUp.
Sweep the sun’s path and visualize shadow envelopes across any day, season, or full year — directly on the model.
Classify entities as sources or receptors and measure exposure with quantifiable outputs, not eyeballed screenshots.
Evaluate photovoltaic potential on any surface using the same solar model as your shadow studies.
Run iterative studies overnight. Compare dozens of massing options without babysitting the tool.
Generate maximum-buildable volumes that respect shadow constraints on neighboring sites.
Layer baseline against variants. Export to CSV for reports, planning submissions, and client reviews.
See the whole day in one glance.

The Shadow Fan visualization overlays shadow positions across a chosen time range onto your model. Check solar access on a public space, sun-hour compliance on a neighboring window, or seasonal exposure on a PV array — without rendering a single frame.
Screenshot: Shadow Fan across Dec 21 showing hourly envelope bands
Data you can put in a report.
Tag neighboring buildings, open space, or individual facades as receptors. Parasolv computes sun-hours, shadow-hours, and overshadowing metrics — then exports clean CSVs for planning submissions.
Screenshot: Receptor panel with per-receptor sun-hour breakdown + gradient overlay
For when one study isn’t enough.

The Studio tier adds batch processing and design-envelope generation — so you can explore dozens of massing options, or back-solve the largest building the site can support without overshadowing its neighbors.
Screenshot: Design envelope solid generated from shadow constraints
Download the plugin, run a shadow study on your own model, and decide from there. No card required for the free Lite tier.
Each module below corresponds to a panel in the plugin. Tier badges show where each capability lives.

Tag model entities as sources (shadow casters) or receptors (the surfaces you care about). Configure location, date ranges, and grid resolution once — Parasolv remembers it for the rest of your study.

The core of the plugin. Sweep the sun across any day or season and see the shadow envelope live on your model. Tune gradient, opacity, and banding from the Graphics panel without leaving the workflow.
Evaluate photovoltaic potential on any face using the same solar model as your shadow studies. Great for early-stage feasibility on roofs, facades, and canopies.
Batch runs a queue of configurations end-to-end. Mask Mode hides non-essential geometry during analysis to speed up heavy models. Studio users can schedule batches to run overnight.
Back-solve the largest volume a site can support without overshadowing defined receptors. Export the envelope as a SketchUp group for massing studies and feasibility reports.
Layer variants on top of a baseline. Compare receptor-level metrics at a glance, then export structured CSVs ready for planning submissions, compliance reports, or client markdown.

Which SketchUp version does Parasolv support?
SketchUp 2026 and later on both Windows and macOS (Apple Silicon). Older versions are not supported.

From install to first study in 15 minutes.
Pick the track that fits you. Architect is written for anyone comfortable in SketchUp. Studio dives deeper into methodology and advanced workflows.
Download Parasolv from your account page, double-click the .rbz, and restart SketchUp. The Parasolv panel appears in the Extensions menu.
Screenshot: SketchUp extensions menu with Parasolv highlighted
Open the Setup panel, confirm the model location, and choose the day (or range) you want to analyze. Parasolv uses SketchUp’s native geolocation so you don’t need to re-enter it.
Screenshot: Setup panel with location + date selector

Tag buildings and obstructions as sources, and the surfaces you care about (neighboring facades, public space, gardens) as receptors. Think of it as telling the plugin “what’s casting shadow” vs. “what you’re measuring.”
Screenshot: Classifier panel with entity list + coloured preview
Hit Run. Shadow Fan overlays appear on the model within seconds for a single day; a full-year study takes a minute or two depending on receptor count.
Screenshot: Model with live Shadow Fan overlay
The Results panel lists each receptor with sun-hours and shadow-hours. The gradient overlay on the model shows where exposure is highest and lowest at a glance.
Screenshot: Results panel with receptor table + gradient legend
Pro and Studio tiers export CSVs ready for planning submissions or client decks. Lite users can screenshot the viewport overlay.
Screenshot: CSV preview with per-receptor metrics

Studio users should tune grid resolution before running compliance studies. As a rule of thumb: 0.25 m for facade receptors where local planning guidance requires sub-metre accuracy, 1.0 m for open-space studies. See the methodology reference for per-jurisdiction notes.
Screenshot: Analysis Settings with grid resolution + timestep controls

Queue multiple massing variants in one run. Each entry can override the source set, date range, or envelope constraints. Batches serialize to JSON — check them into your project repo for reproducibility.
Screenshot: Batch configuration JSON with queued scenarios

Define the shadow constraint (e.g. “≥ 2 hrs sun on Mar 21, 10:00–16:00, on this facade”), then generate the maximum-buildable volume that satisfies it. The result is a SketchUp solid you can union with your site boundary for developable-area studies.
Screenshot: Envelope generation with constraint dialog

Layer any number of scenarios over a baseline. The comparison view highlights deltas per receptor — useful for planning appeals where you need to demonstrate that a scheme does not degrade existing conditions.
Screenshot: Scenario diff view with +/- deltas per receptor

PV output estimates use clear-sky irradiance combined with the Parasolv solar model. Calibrate against TMY data for your region if you need compliance-grade numbers; otherwise the default profile is good for feasibility-stage estimates.
Screenshot: PV surface heatmap with irradiance legend
Exported CSVs follow a documented schema: receptor_id, date, sun_hours, shadow_hours, met_criteria. Hook them into Excel, Grasshopper, or Python for bespoke reporting pipelines.
Screenshot: CSV schema reference with column definitions
